coverage: No conformance fixture has more than three task.async sites; none spawns more than four total tasks. Largest available runnable task fixtures were measured as controls. The benchmark task user is the resource-drops correctness control; no sealed workload benchmark spawns tasks.
verdict: Ordered commit does not reach 1.5x at four workers: the app predicts about 1.02x at light load and 1.04x under a backlog. The backlog trace spends about 97.9% of model time stalled at the head while a later result is ready, with about 0.4% commit busy time. Serial dependencies and long-head stalls dominate, rather than commit throughput. Rank the free-running prototype ahead of ordered commit under the brief threshold, while measuring its mutex contention separately. These are conditional compute projections, not measured multicore throughput.
limitations: N segment workers plus a separate serial commit server, including at N=1.
Host I/O latency is excluded; readiness dependencies follow the observed run.
No cache transfer, worker handoff, or deferred-count cost is modelled.
Measurement heap accounting and monotonic timers perturb short segments; perf ratios quantify profiler overhead, not multicore speedup.
SMT sibling activity was high and is retained per sample; every speedup is within one trace and no absolute cross-session timing comparison is used.
